R5B-bear-walk-0001.name: 2.9 km N of Hotnarko Lake
R5B-bear-walk-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R5B-bear-walk-0001.parkWhat: pull off on C3886 Spur 5 (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2019 (7 years old), 220 m N: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2021 (fire C51355), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 10 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 120 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

R5B-camp-camp-0003.recDirections: From Anahim Lake, travel south on Kappan Mountain Road (the turnoff is just west of the Anahim Lake Airport). Travel 5 km and turn right onto the Beeftrail Main Forest Service Road. Travel 11.7 km and turn left. Travel 1.7 km and turn right onto the access road. Continue approximately 7.0 km on very rough road to the recreation site. The road is extremely rough with seasonal flooding, vehicle access is limited to 4-wheel drive vehicles with adequate clearance.
